When the other reel ran out, you were talking about your aunt.

Augusta Glover, yes. And she said that she was a very dear friend to Leon Rene's wife, the Renes, both of them, for that matter. They happened to have been neighbors and friends, and she suggested, she said, 'I want you to meet Mr. Rene.' she said, 'and I think he can help you.' And she went raving about -- well, I had known of their reputation, you know, and she said, 'I'm going to call him and ask him if he would listen to some of your songs.' Well, I -- you know, she knew that I wrote songs, you know, and she said, 'He has his own little recording company.' Leon, at that time did have. I don't remember the name of the little company, but he had a little company at that time. And she said, 'He may be able to help you, to record you or something.' And she said, 'Would you like to?' I said, 'I would love to, I would love to meet him.'

So she made an appointment for me with Leon Rene and I went down to his home and he heard, you know, some of the things that I was doing, plus some of the little arrangements that I had done for myself, vocal arrangements, you know. And he wasn't too excited.

He wasn't too excited. He said, 'Well, that's nice.' He says, 'Well, yeah, that's nice.' And he says, 'Well, I tell you what, right now I don't have any calls for what you're doing right now,' but he says, 'I tell you, if I find a way I can help you, I'll give you a call.' So that was the end of that. And I never did see him anymore or hear from him anymore until the March of Dimes show, which is the show where I was discovered. This was at the Hollywood High School in Hollywood. And when he came to this affair that night, well I guess everybody was there, and my little son was instrumental in encouraging me and getting his mom to do this show. And it was a big thing and Bob Hope, Barbara Hutton, and God knows who else wasn't there. I don't -- Betty, I don't mean Barbara Hutton. I meant Betty Hutton, I'm sorry. And he says, 'Momma, all the kids are going to be at the Hollywood High School for the March of Dimes.' The March of Dimes was a big thing. Do you remember that?
